dimensions.assessment: Affects banking institutions, regulatory agencies (Federal Reserve and CFPB), and all consumers or depositors making check deposits and wire transfers.
dimensions.evidence: receiving banks are allowed to delay the processing of checks or wire transfers that they reasonably suspect are fraudulent.

dimensions.assessment: Allows holds on funds for up to 45 or 60 days and waives overdraft fees under specific notice conditions.
dimensions.evidence: an initial hold that is not to exceed 10 days and an extended hold that is not to exceed 45 days.

dimensions.assessment: Requires studies and reports on fraud losses and funds availability but does not specify direct federal expenditures.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study of...

dimensions.assessment: Alters federal fund availability rules and mandates joint rulemaking by the Federal Reserve Board and the CFPB.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Expedited Funds Availability Act to provide exceptions in the case of fraudulent checks or wire transfers, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory exceptions and regulatory authority for depository institutions.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by section 3(a)(3) and section 4 shall take effect 60 days after the rules described in subsection (a) are adopted.

missing_information: Specific data on the volume or dollar amount of delayed funds nationwide.
importance_detail.rationale: Amends the Expedited Funds Availability Act to permit banks to place holds on deposited checks and wire transfers suspected of fraud, impacting banking operations and consumer fund availability.
